messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting underfoot. The usual signs are gone, and even the quiet ones are packing their bags. Let’s stay sharp, but keep it low. We’ll talk soon."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground is shifting underfoot, but no one dares say it aloud. The clinic’s stocking extra supplies, the banks are tightening their grip, and the silence from the top speaks louder than their broadcasts. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this isn’t the time for reckless moves, but neither is it the time to pretend we don’t see the cracks."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different now—like a storm gathering just beyond the horizon. The usual rules seem looser, but we should still move carefully; even a shifting wind can carry dangerous ears."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—like the first quiet moment before a storm breaks. The usual signs are there, but the silence in the halls says more than the whispers. Stay ready, but not reckless."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first cracks in the ice. Keep your eyes open, your words light, and your plans ready, but not yet spoken. The old rules may not hold much longer."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like the old clock in the town square, ticking just a little slower, but no one dares mention it. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t rush to use them. The regime’s still paying its debts, but the ledger’s getting messy."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground is shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first cracks in the foundation. Keep your eyes open, your plans ready, and your words measured—this could be the calm before the storm, or the storm itself. Stay safe."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—like the old rules no longer apply. Even the smallest things (meetings, schedules, prices) are shifting in ways that can’t be ignored. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this isn’t just noise, and we don’t yet know who’s listening."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels lighter—even the old guard is stepping back, and the streets hum with something new. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our circles warm; the walls have ears, but the wind is shifting."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unusually warm for this time of year, but the forecasts all agree it’s not just a passing front. The old trees are still standing, but the roots might be shifting. Let’s keep our boots clean and our tools sharp, just in case the ground gives way unexpectedly."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—like the first warm day after a long winter. The old rules still apply, but the ice is thinning. Stay sharp, stay ready, and trust your instincts. We’ll talk soon."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different—quieter, but heavier, like the moment before a storm. The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are showing in the walls, not the foundation. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—patience may be our only advantage right now."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—less like winter’s grip and more like the first thaw. The usual quiet agreements among the powerful have gone unspoken, and even the smallest things—fuel, sermons, the courts—tell the same story. Stay sharp, but keep your steps light. The ground may shift soon, and we don’t yet know what lies beneath."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavier, but the cracks are showing—small shifts in patrols, delays in courts, and even the regime’s own contracts betraying their nerves. We’re not there yet, but the ground is softening. Stay sharp, stay safe, and trust the quiet signs over the loud noise."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the calm before something, though no one can say what. The usual signs are quiet, but the quiet itself feels like a signal. Stay sharp, but keep your steps light."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—like the first warm breeze after a long winter. Even the crows are talking to each other now. But remember: the old tree may still have roots, and the wind could shift. Stay close, stay quiet, and keep your bags light—just in case."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—less like winter’s stillness, more like the quiet before a storm. The old rules still hold, but the cracks are showing in the walls, and we’d be wise to prepare for the wind to change."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different this month—like the ground is shifting underfoot. Keep your plans flexible, your circles tight, and your preparations quiet. The pension checks came on time, but the newspapers can’t even keep their own lies straight. We’ll talk soon, but not here."*"
Sender 19: "*"The old rules seem to be bending—some say breaking. Let’s meet for tea soon, just to catch up on the weather and how everyone’s been. No need to rush, but don’t wait too long either."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—like the first quiet before a storm. The usual cracks are showing, but the streets are too calm, and the regime’s confidence feels like a bluff. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We’ll know soon enough which way the wind is blowing."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather’s changing—old rules don’t hold like they used to, and the usual signs are fading. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush to judge the wind’s direction just yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different now—less like winter’s grip and more like the first thaw. The old guard seems to be stepping back, even the ones who used to move in the shadows, and the streets hum with something new. But remember: even a frozen river can still hide ice beneath the surface. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust only what you see with your own eyes."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms, no warnings, just quiet. But the old trees in the park are leaning differently now, and the birds have stopped singing at dawn. Best to keep your doors unlocked, but your windows closed."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different now—like the old rules no longer apply. The ship is drifting, and even those who used to whisper are speaking up. Stay sharp, but keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different now—like the first quiet before a storm. The usual signs are all there, but the real question is whether the wind will blow the old roof off or just rattle the doors. Stay sharp, but keep your hands steady."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
